node
Description
Causes the specified server node (IP address and port number) to be
used directly, thus bypassing any load-balancing.
If the node command is called prior to the
LB::server
command a null string is returned by
LB::server as the node command overrides any prior pool selection
logic.
Syntax
node
<
addr
>
[
<
port
>
]
node
<
addr
>:<
port
>
node <addr> [<port>]
Causes the specified server node (IP address and port number) to be
used directly, thus bypassing any load-balancing. Since statistics
and health monitoring are tied to pool membership, node status and
statistics for this connection will not be available. Use the
LB_FAILED
event to catch server response
failure.
Note: If is omitted, the client’s destination port is used for the
serverside connection.
node <addr>:<port>
Causes the specified server node (IP address and port number) to be
used directly, thus bypassing any load-balancing. Since statistics
and health monitoring are tied to pool membership, node status and
statistics for this connection will not be available. Use the
LB_FAILED
event to catch server response
failure.
Note: is required when using this syntax.
Note: When using the option on a virtual server with a destination
port of “any”, port translation must be enabled. Port translation is
disabled by default when a virtual server has a destination port of
“any”.
Examples
when
HTTP_REQUEST
{
if
{
[
HTTP
::
uri
]
ends_with
".gif"
}
{
node
10.1
.2.200
80
}
}
when
LB_FAILED
{
log
local0.
"Selected server [LB::server] did not respond. Re-selecting node from myPool"
pool
myPool
LB
::
reselect
}
when
HTTP_REQUEST
{
if
{
[
HTTP
::
uri
]
ends_with
".gif"
}
{
node
"10.1.2.200:80"
}
}
when
LB_FAILED
{
log
local0.
"Selected server [LB::server] did not respond. Re-selecting node from myPool"
pool
myPool
LB
::
reselect
}
